meta.trial_name: JUPITER (Justification for the Use of Statins in Prevention: an Intervention Trial Evaluating Rosuvastatin)
meta.mechanism: HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor (statin); lowers LDL-C ~50% and, in JUPITER, also lowered hsCRP ~37% (the trial's enrichment biomarker)
meta.indication: primary prevention of first major cardiovascular events in apparently healthy men >=50 and women >=60 years with LDL-C <130 mg/dL and hsCRP >=2.0 mg/L, without diabetes or prior cardiovascular disease

n_randomized.quote: We randomly assigned 17,802 apparently healthy men and women with low-density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol levels of less than 130 mg per deciliter (3.4 mmol per liter) and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein levels of 2.0 mg per liter or higher to rosuvastatin, 20 mg daily, or placebo
n_randomized.note: 8901 per arm (Table 1). Registry S3 enrollment count 17802 (ACTUAL).

median_followup.quote: The trial was stopped after a median follow-up of 1.9 years (maximum, 5.0).
median_followup.note: Hlatky editorial S6: stopped 'with only 1.9 of its proposed 4 years of follow-up concluded'. Mora S9 says the trial 'was expected to last approximately five years'.

primary_endpoint.value: First major cardiovascular event: nonfatal MI, nonfatal stroke, hospitalization for unstable angina, arterial revascularization, or confirmed death from cardiovascular causes
primary_endpoint.quote: The primary outcome was the occurrence of a first major cardiovascular event, defined as nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, hospitalization for unstable angina, an arterial revascularization procedure, or confirmed death from cardiovascular causes.
primary_endpoint.note: Registry S3 primary outcome is the same composite.

inclusion_key_criteria.value: Men >=50 y, women >=60 y; no history of cardiovascular disease; LDL-C <130 mg/dL; hsCRP >=2.0 mg/L; TG <500 mg/dL; excluded prior lipid-lowering therapy, diabetes, uncontrolled hypertension, cancer within 5 y, inflammatory conditions, immunosuppressants; 4-week placebo run-in with >80% compliance
inclusion_key_criteria.quote: men 50 years of age or older and women 60 years of age or older were eligible for the trial if they did not have a history of cardiovascular disease and if, at the initial screening visit, they had an LDL cholesterol level of less than 130 mg per deciliter (3.4 mmol per liter) and a high-sensitivity C-reactive protein level of 2.0 mg per liter or more.
inclusion_key_criteria.note: TG limit: 'a triglyceride level of less than 500 mg per deciliter (5.6 mmol per liter)'. 89,890 screened; 37,611 excluded for LDL-C >=130 and 25,993 for hsCRP <2.0 mg/L. No low-hsCRP arm (see open_questions).

planned_events.quote: JUPITER was an event-driven trial designed to continue until 520 confirmed primary end points had been documented, to provide a statistical power of 90% to detect a 25% reduction in the rate of the primary end point, with a two-sided significance level of 0.05.
planned_events.note: Trial stopped at the first prespecified interim efficacy analysis with 393 primary events in the final ITT count (142+251). A search snippet of the AstraZeneca clinical study report synopsis said 328 endpoints had been adjudicated at the time of the recommendation; that document returned HTTP 403 and was not read (unverified).

assumed_rrr.quote: JUPITER was an event-driven trial designed to continue until 520 confirmed primary end points had been documented, to provide a statistical power of 90% to detect a 25% reduction in the rate of the primary end point, with a two-sided significance level of 0.05.

power.quote: JUPITER was an event-driven trial designed to continue until 520 confirmed primary end points had been documented, to provide a statistical power of 90% to detect a 25% reduction in the rate of the primary end point, with a two-sided significance level of 0.05.

alpha.quote: JUPITER was an event-driven trial designed to continue until 520 confirmed primary end points had been documented, to provide a statistical power of 90% to detect a 25% reduction in the rate of the primary end point, with a two-sided significance level of 0.05.
alpha.note: Monitoring plan: 'two interim efficacy analyses with O'Brien-Fleming stopping boundaries determined by means of the Lan-DeMets approach'.

stopped_early.quote: The stopping boundary was crossed at the first prespecified efficacy evaluation, and on March 29, 2008, the independent data and safety monitoring board voted to recommend termination of the trial.
stopped_early.note: Reason: efficacy (benefit). Press release S2 (2008-03-31): 'The study will be stopped early because there is unequivocal evidence of a reduction in cardiovascular morbidity and mortality amongst patients who received CRESTOR when compared to placebo.' Trial ended March 30, 2008 when the steering committee accepted the recommendation.

baseline.quote: In both the rosuvastatin and placebo groups, the median LDL cholesterol level was 108 mg per deciliter (2.8 mmol per liter)
baseline.note: 2.8 mmol/L; IQR 94-119 (Table 1). Also in pre-readout baseline paper S5 (epub 2007-10-24): 'median 108 mg/dl, interquartile range 94 to 119'. Friedewald LDL-C (method per S9).

baseline.quote: the high-sensitivity C-reactive protein level was 4.2 and 4.3 mg per liter in the rosuvastatin and placebo groups, respectively.
baseline.note: hsCRP = average of two screening visits; IQR 2.8-7.1 / 2.8-7.2.

baseline.quote: the high-density lipoprotein (HDL) cholesterol level was 49 mg per deciliter (1.3 mmol per liter), and the triglyceride level was 118 mg per deciliter (1.3 mmol per liter)
The apolipoprotein B levels were not low (median baseline concentration 109 mg/dL).
baseline.note: Subset of 7,832 rosuvastatin-allocated participants with baseline and 1-year measures (not whole trial). Immunonephelometry (Behring).

baseline.quote: the total cholesterol, LDL-C, and non-HDL cholesterol were all low (respective median baseline concentrations of 186, 108, and 134 mg/dL).

baseline.note: NOT SEARCHED IN DEPTH: Lp(a) not reported in S1; JUPITER Lp(a) analyses exist (Khera et al. 2014) but were not read. Not relevant to the statin mechanism.

biomarker_effects.method: Friedewald calculated LDL-C (ultracentrifugation if TG >=400 mg/dL), central laboratory (method per S9)
biomarker_effects.quote: At the 12-month visit, the rosuvastatin group, as compared with the placebo group, had a 50% lower median LDL cholesterol level (mean difference, 47 mg per deciliter [1.2 mmol per liter]), a 37% lower median high-sensitivity C-reactive protein level, and a 17% lower median triglyceride level (P<0.001 for all three comparisons).
biomarker_effects.location: Results, Compliance and Effects of Rosuvastatin
biomarker_effects.note: -50% is the difference in medians; -47 mg/dL is the mean between-group difference. Median on-treatment LDL-C 55 mg/dL vs 110 placebo at 12 months (Table 2), maintained at 24-48 months (53-55 vs 106-109). 75% of participants were taking study pills at termination.

biomarker_effects.quote: a 50% lower median LDL cholesterol level (mean difference, 47 mg per deciliter [1.2 mmol per liter])
biomarker_effects.note: CTT check (derived, not from source): 0.79^1.2 = 0.75 expected over ~5 years vs observed HR 0.56 at median 1.9 years. Authors (S1 Discussion): expected ~25% reduction; observed 'almost twice this magnitude'.

biomarker_effects.quote: At the 12-month visit, the rosuvastatin group, as compared with the placebo group, had a 50% lower median LDL cholesterol level (mean difference, 47 mg per deciliter [1.2 mmol per liter]), a 37% lower median high-sensitivity C-reactive protein level, and a 17% lower median triglyceride level (P<0.001 for all three comparisons).
biomarker_effects.location: Results, Compliance and Effects of Rosuvastatin
biomarker_effects.note: Difference in medians: 2.2 vs 3.5 mg/L at 12 months (Table 2). Abstract: 'Rosuvastatin reduced LDL cholesterol levels by 50% and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein levels by 37%.' CRP is not causal by Mendelian randomization (S21-S23).

biomarker_effects.quote: At the 12-month visit, the rosuvastatin group, as compared with the placebo group, had a 50% lower median LDL cholesterol level (mean difference, 47 mg per deciliter [1.2 mmol per liter]), a 37% lower median high-sensitivity C-reactive protein level, and a 17% lower median triglyceride level (P<0.001 for all three comparisons).
biomarker_effects.location: Results, Compliance and Effects of Rosuvastatin

biomarker_effects.quote: At 12 months, the median HDL cholesterol level was 4% higher in the rosuvastatin group than in the placebo group (P<0.001), but this effect was not present at the time of study completion (P = 0.34).
biomarker_effects.location: Results, Compliance and Effects of Rosuvastatin

biomarker_effects.quote: Random allocation to rosuvastatin in the JUPITER trial decreased median on-treatment concentrations of total, LDL, and non-HDL-C to a similar extent on a mass concentration scale (−50 mg/dL, −50 mg/dL, and −54 mg/dL, respectively) and reduced apolipoprotein B by 41 mg/dL ( Table 1 ). There was greater proportional LDL-C lowering (46.2%) compared with non-HDL-C (40.3%) or apolipoprotein B (37.6%) with rosuvastatin therapy.
biomarker_effects.note: NOT placebo-adjusted: change from baseline within 7,832 rosuvastatin-treated participants (109 -> 66 mg/dL). Placebo-adjusted apoB change NOT FOUND. Placebo-arm LDL-C was roughly flat (108 -> 110 mg/dL, S1 Table 2), so within-arm change approximates the placebo-adjusted effect.

biomarker_effects.quote: There was greater proportional LDL-C lowering (46.2%) compared with non-HDL-C (40.3%) or apolipoprotein B (37.6%) with rosuvastatin therapy.
biomarker_effects.note: NOT placebo-adjusted (within-arm, 134 -> 76 mg/dL). -54 mg/dL = -1.40 mmol/L (derived). Placebo-adjusted non-HDL-C NOT FOUND.

biomarker_effects.quote: Rosuvastatin was associated with highly significant dose-dependent reductions in LDL cholesterol compared with placebo (p <0.001); decreases ranged from 34% (1 mg) to 65% (80 mg).
biomarker_effects.note: Phase 2 in hypercholesterolaemia (n=142 + 64), published 2001 (before readout). The 20 mg arm value is not given in the abstract (change_pct null). Abstract also: 'an additional 4.5% LDL cholesterol reduction for each doubling of the rosuvastatin dose'.

biomarker_effects.timepoint: 2 years (METEOR, rosuvastatin 40 mg, low-risk primary prevention)
biomarker_effects.quote: Among participants in the rosuvastatin group, the mean (SD) baseline LDL cholesterol level of 155 (24.1) mg/dL declined to 78 (27.5) mg/dL, a mean reduction of 49% (P<.001 vs placebo group).
biomarker_effects.note: Pre-readout (2007-03-25) placebo-controlled trial at 40 mg (not 20 mg); 49% is within-arm change. Pre-readout baseline paper S5 also states '20 mg of rosuvastatin can reduce LDL cholesterol by up to 50%'.

hr.quote: The rates of the primary end point were 0.77 and 1.36 per 100 person-years of follow-up in the rosuvastatin and placebo groups, respectively (hazard ratio for rosuvastatin, 0.56; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.46 to 0.69; P<0.00001)
hr.note: MI HR 0.46 (0.30-0.70); stroke HR 0.52 (0.34-0.79); revascularization or unstable angina HR 0.53 (0.40-0.70); MI, stroke or CV death HR 0.53 (0.40-0.69); death from any cause HR 0.80 (0.67-0.97), P=0.02. Registry S3: HR 0.56 (0.46-0.69), p<0.0001 (Cox).

ci_low.quote: hazard ratio for rosuvastatin, 0.56; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.46 to 0.69

ci_high.quote: hazard ratio for rosuvastatin, 0.56; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.46 to 0.69

p.quote: hazard ratio for rosuvastatin, 0.56; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.46 to 0.69; P<0.00001

events_treatment.quote: 142 first major cardiovascular events had occurred in the rosuvastatin group, as compared with 251 in the placebo group (Table 3).

events_control.quote: 142 first major cardiovascular events had occurred in the rosuvastatin group, as compared with 251 in the placebo group (Table 3).

safety_signals.value: Physician-reported new diabetes higher with rosuvastatin: 270 (3.0%) vs 216 (2.4%), P=0.01; median HbA1c 5.9% vs 5.8% at 24 months (P=0.001)
safety_signals.quote: Nevertheless, physician-reported diabetes was more frequent in the rosuvastatin group (270 reports of diabetes, vs. 216 in the placebo group; P = 0.01); these events were not adjudicated by the end-point committee.
safety_signals.note: Ridker 2012 (S11): HR 1.25 (1.05-1.49), p=0.01; excess confined to participants with >=1 diabetes risk factor. Later judged an on-target class effect: Sattar 2010 (S20) statins OR 1.09 (1.02-1.17); HMGCR genetics (S19).

safety_signals.value: No excess myopathy (10 vs 9), newly diagnosed cancer (298 vs 314) or ALT >3x ULN (23 vs 17); cancer deaths fewer (35 vs 58, P=0.02)
safety_signals.quote: There were no significant differences between the two study groups with regard to muscle weakness, newly diagnosed cancer, or disorders of the hematologic, gastrointestinal, hepatic, or renal systems.
safety_signals.note: One rhabdomyolysis case after trial closure.

safety_signals.value: No excess intracranial / hemorrhagic stroke: 6 vs 9 (P=0.44)
safety_signals.quote: we found no significant between-group difference in the number of subjects with intracranial hemorrhage (six in the rosuvastatin group and nine in the placebo group, P = 0.44).
Total numbers of reported serious adverse events were similar in the rosuvastatin and placebo groups (1352 and 1377, respectively; P = 0.60) (Table 4).

genetics.finding: HMGCR LDL-lowering genetic scores protect against cardiovascular events per unit LDL-C, equal to PCSK9; same scores raise diabetes risk
genetics.effect: OR 0.81 (0.72-0.90) per 10 mg/dL lower LDL-C for HMGCR score; diabetes OR 1.13 (1.06-1.20)
genetics.quote: odds ratio for cardiovascular events, 0.81 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.74 to 0.89) for PCSK9 and 0.81 (95% CI, 0.72 to 0.90) for HMGCR

genetics.finding: HMGCR variants (rs17238484, rs12916) lower LDL-C and raise bodyweight, glucose, insulin and type 2 diabetes risk: statin diabetes excess is at least partly on-target
genetics.effect: rs12916-T T2D OR 1.06 (1.03-1.09) per allele; statin trials new-onset T2D OR 1.12 (1.06-1.18)
genetics.quote: The increased risk of type 2 diabetes noted with statins is at least partially explained by HMGCR inhibition.

genetics.finding: LDL-C is causal; CTT 2005 (pre-readout): about one-fifth fewer major vascular events per 1 mmol/L LDL-C reduction over ~5 years
genetics.effect: RR 0.79 (0.77-0.81) per 1.0 mmol/L for major vascular events
genetics.quote: Statin therapy can safely reduce the 5-year incidence of major coronary events, coronary revascularisation, and stroke by about one fifth per mmol/L reduction in LDL cholesterol, largely irrespective of the initial lipid profile or other presenting characteristics.

genetics.finding: CRP is not causal: CRP gene variants raising CRP up to 64% were not associated with ischemic vascular disease (Copenhagen studies)
genetics.effect: no association of CRP genotypes with ischemic heart or cerebrovascular disease
genetics.quote: However, these polymorphisms are not in themselves associated with an increased risk of ischemic vascular disease.

genetics.finding: Mendelian randomization of CRP-locus variants (28,112 cases) shows no association with CHD; argues against causal CRP
genetics.effect: OR 1.00 (0.97-1.02) per 20% lower CRP vs 0.94 predicted from observational data
genetics.quote: The lack of concordance between the effect on coronary heart disease risk of CRP genotypes and CRP levels argues against a causal association of CRP with coronary heart disease.

genetics.finding: CCGC individual-participant Mendelian randomization (194,418 participants): genetically raised CRP not associated with CHD
genetics.effect: RR 1.00 (0.90-1.13) per 1 SD higher genetically raised ln CRP vs 1.33 (1.23-1.43) observational
genetics.quote: Human genetic data indicate that C reactive protein concentration itself is unlikely to be even a modest causal factor in coronary heart disease.

consensus_explanation.summary: JUPITER clearly met its primary endpoint: rosuvastatin 20 mg cut first major cardiovascular events by 44% (142 vs 251 events; HR 0.56, 95% CI 0.46-0.69) after the trial was stopped for benefit at its first interim analysis, and the FDA approved a primary-prevention indication in 2010. The target (HMGCR) and the main causal biomarker (LDL-C, lowered 50% or 1.2 mmol/L) are validated, so the benefit itself is not in doubt. The first caveat: the effect was about twice the ~25% that the per-mmol/L LDL-C relationship predicts (the authors said so themselves), and Hlatky's editorial says early termination 'probably exaggerated the results to some degree', in line with evidence that truncated trials overestimate effects (Bassler 2010). Second, the hsCRP enrichment strategy could not be tested because there was no low-hsCRP arm, and Mendelian randomization shows CRP itself is not causal, so the extra benefit cannot be credited to CRP lowering. Third, physician-reported diabetes rose (3.0% vs 2.4%, P=0.01), later confirmed as an on-target HMGCR effect, and the absolute benefit over 1.9 years was small (NNT about 120 for hard events); critics (de Lorgeril 2010; Morrissey, Diamond and Kaul 2011) questioned the size of the effect and its policy implications rather than whether the trial was positive.

open_questions: Category choice: robust_success is defensible (upper CI 0.69, every component reduced, FDA approval). success_with_caveats was chosen because the observed effect is about twice what the LDL-C mechanism predicts (authors' own statement), the trial was truncated early (Hlatky: 'probably exaggerated'), and there was a diabetes signal.
Planned follow-up: Hlatky (S6) says 1.9 of a 'proposed 4 years'; Mora (S9) says 'expected to last approximately five years'. Design paper S4 (which would settle it) was not read.

Events at the stopping decision: final ITT count 393 (142+251) vs 520 planned. A search snippet of the AstraZeneca clinical study report synopsis (ctsu.ox.ac.uk, HTTP 403) gave 328 adjudicated endpoints at the time of the recommendation; unverified.
Placebo-adjusted apoB and non-HDL-C changes NOT FOUND (S1 Supplementary Appendix not accessed); within-arm changes from S9 recorded with placebo_adjusted=false.
LDL-C effect: -50% is a difference of medians and -47 mg/dL (1.2 mmol/L) a mean difference at 12 months; 75% adherence at termination, so the ITT effect is diluted.

Role of hsCRP: the investigators (S10) argue that reaching hsCRP <2 mg/L adds benefit, but that is a non-randomized on-treatment analysis; there was no low-hsCRP arm (Hlatky S6, Kaul S13), and CRP Mendelian randomization is null (S21-S23). Whether hsCRP marks risk or modifies statin benefit remains unresolved.
de Lorgeril (S12) raises low CV-to-total mortality ratio and low MI case-fatality as possible bias signals; this minority critique was read in abstract only.
Design paper S4 could not be read (403; Wayback rate-limited), so pre-readout design facts rely on the registry (S3) and baseline paper (S5).
